Poisson model forces variance equal mean, assumption real count data usually violate two ways. First, data often overdispersed: variance exceeds mean unobserved heterogeneity. negative binomial (NB) model handles adding dispersion parameter θ\theta. Second, data often contain zeros even NB model predicts, units never risk positive count. zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model handles mixing NB distribution point mass zero (Lambert, 1992; Cameron Trivedi, 2013). standard R implementations, MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl(), reliable treat estimation black box. goal project build R package, zinbTruitt, fits models first principles reproduces reference implementations. estimation uses closed-form building blocks: iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) regression coefficients, Newton–Raphson dispersion parameter, EM algorithm (Dempster, Laird Rubin, 1977) zero-inflation mixture. call optim() general-purpose optimizer made. report describes algorithms (Section 2), package (Section 3), agreement reference functions two data sets (Section 4), simulation study (Section 5), analysis physician office visits 1987–88 National Medical Expenditure Survey (Section 6), limitations (Section 7). numbers, tables, figures produced code document calls installed package.

what: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression via IRLS and EM
title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression via IRLS and EM
text: zinbTruitt fits count-data regression models without general-purpose optimizer (optim() friends never called): nbreg(): negative binomial (NB2) regression, using IRLS (Fisher scoring) coefficients alternated Newton-Raphson dispersion theta. Comparable MASS::glm.nb(). zinbreg(): zero-inflated negative binomial regression, using EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits. Standard errors come observed information matrix. Comparable pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin"). Developed STA 651 Final Project (Fall 2026), Miami University. Website report: https://JosephTruitt.github.io/zinbTruitt/
